blocks.text: Imagine you own a small shop in Lagos. How do you keep track of all the cash and bank transactions daily?

blocks.markdown: In accounting, the cash book is a crucial tool used to record all cash and bank transactions. It serves as both a journal and a ledger, making it an essential part of the books of original entry.

blocks.title: Cash Book
blocks.text: A cash book is a financial journal that contains all cash receipts and payments, including bank deposits and withdrawals.

blocks.markdown: There are two main types of cash books: the two-column cash book and the three-column cash book. The two-column cash book records cash and bank transactions, while the three-column cash book also includes a column for discounts.

blocks.title: Recording in a Two-Column Cash Book
blocks.prompt:
Record the following transactions in a two-column cash book: 
1. Cash sales of ₦10,000 
2. Paid ₦5,000 into the bank 
3. Received ₦2,000 from a debtor

steps.text: Enter the cash sales of ₦10,000 on the debit side under the cash column.
Record the payment of ₦5,000 into the bank on the credit side under the cash column and debit the bank column.
Enter the receipt of ₦2,000 from a debtor on the debit side under the cash column.

blocks.answer: The cash book will show a cash balance of ₦7,000 and a bank balance of ₦5,000.

blocks.markdown: In a three-column cash book, the discount columns are used to record discounts allowed and received. This helps in tracking reductions in the amounts payable or receivable.

blocks.title: Contra Entry
blocks.text: A contra entry involves both the cash and bank columns. It occurs when cash is deposited into or withdrawn from the bank.

points: A cash book records all cash and bank transactions.
Two-column cash books include cash and bank columns.
Three-column cash books also include discount columns.
Contra entries affect both cash and bank columns.
